findings.title: Reentrancy
findings.description: The withdraw function allows for reentrancy attacks because it makes an external call to msg.sender before updating the state variable balances.
findings.recommendation: Use the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern by updating the state variable balances before making the external call.

findings.title: Unprotected Function
findings.description: The deposit function is not protected against potential front-running attacks, allowing an attacker to manipulate the contract's state.

findings.title: Unsecured Use of Transfer
findings.description: The use of the transfer function (via msg.sender.call{value: bal}()) in the withdraw function can lead to issues if the recipient contract does not handle the transfer correctly.

findings.title: reentrancy-eth
findings.description:
Reentrancy in SampleVault.withdraw() (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#14-20):
	External calls:
	- (ok,None) = msg.sender.call{value: bal}() (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#17)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- balances[msg.sender] = 0 (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#19)
	SampleVault.balances (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#7) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- SampleVault.balances (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#7)
	- SampleVault.deposit() (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#9-11)
	- SampleVault.withdraw() (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#14-20)

findings.title: low-level-calls
findings.description:
Low level call in SampleVault.withdraw() (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#14-20):
	- (ok,None) = msg.sender.call{value: bal}() (contracts/audit-targets/SampleVault.sol#17)

findings.title: Oracle Manipulation
findings.description: The contract does not check for the freshness of the price data or ensure that the price is from the latest round.
findings.recommendation: Implement checks to ensure that the price data is fresh and from the latest round, such as verifying that 'updatedAt' is recent and 'answeredInRound' is greater than or equal to 'roundId'.

findings.title: Unprotected Function
findings.description: The function 'getPrice' is marked as external view but does not have any access control or restrictions, potentially allowing it to be called by anyone.

findings.title: Integer Overflow
findings.description: The function 'valueOf' performs multiplication of 'amount' and 'answer' which could potentially cause an integer overflow if the result is larger than the maximum value that can be stored in a uint256.

findings.title: unused-return
findings.description: UnsafeOracle.valueOf(uint256) (contracts/audit-targets/UnsafeOracle.sol#26-29) ignores return value by (None,answer,None,None,None) = feed.latestRoundData() (contracts/audit-targets/UnsafeOracle.sol#27)

findings.title: unused-return
findings.description: UnsafeOracle.getPrice() (contracts/audit-targets/UnsafeOracle.sol#19-24) ignores return value by (None,answer,None,None,None) = feed.latestRoundData() (contracts/audit-targets/UnsafeOracle.sol#21)

findings.title: oracle-no-staleness
findings.description: Oracle read in UnsafeOracle.valueOf(uint256) (contracts/audit-targets/UnsafeOracle.sol#26-29) has no staleness check. Validate updatedAt / publishTime / answeredInRound.

findings.title: solc-version
findings.description:
Version constraint ^0.8.19 contains known severe issues (https://solidity.readthedocs.io/en/latest/bugs.html)
	- VerbatimInvalidDeduplication
	- FullInlinerNonExpressionSplitArgumentEvaluationOrder
	- MissingSideEffectsOnSelectorAccess.
It is used by:
	- ^0.8.19 (contracts/audit-targets/UnsafeOracle.sol#2)

findings.title: Delegatecall Injection
findings.description: The fallback function uses delegatecall to forward calls to the implementation contract. If the implementation contract is malicious, it can manipulate the state of the ProxyAdmin contract.
findings.recommendation: Implement checks to ensure that the new implementation contract is trusted and follows the expected interface. Consider using a whitelist of approved implementations.

findings.title: Admin Control
findings.description: The admin can change the implementation contract and the admin address, which could lead to a complete takeover of the contract if the admin key is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Implement a multi-signature wallet for admin functions or a time-lock mechanism for critical changes.

findings.title: locked-ether
findings.description:
Contract locking ether found:
	Contract ProxyAdmin (contracts/audit-targets/ProxyAdmin.sol#6-64) has payable functions:
	 - ProxyAdmin.fallback() (contracts/audit-targets/ProxyAdmin.sol#44-54)
	 - ProxyAdmin.receive() (contracts/audit-targets/ProxyAdmin.sol#56)
	But does not have a function to withdraw the ether
